Script Task

General Concept: A Script Task in BPMN is used to execute a script or code fragment as part of a process. It is typically used for simple data manipulation, calculations, or custom logic that does not require external integration.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Script Task runs a script using the configured script engine. Input and output mappings can be defined using FEEL expressions. Script Tasks operate within the process scope, and can read and write mapped variables. Error handling is supported, and scripts should be designed to fail gracefully. The engine supports multiple scripting languages, depending on configuration.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Script Task in TaktX allows you to:

  • Execute scripts or code fragments for data transformation, calculations, or custom logic.
  • Configure input and output mappings using FEEL expressions for flexible data transformation.
  • Define scripts to perform calculations, data transformations, or business logic.
  • Integrate with process variables and use FEEL for script expressions.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Attach boundary events for error or timer handling.

 

Example: Discount Calculation with Script Task

 

This example shows a process where an order is received, a Script Task calculates a discount, and the process continues to approval. The Script Task demonstrates automated business logic within the process.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions for flexible data mapping.
  • Keep scripts simple and focused on process logic.
  • Handle errors gracefully within the script.
  • Document script purpose and expected inputs/outputs.

Pitfalls:

  • Complex scripts can be hard to maintain and debug.
  • Unmapped variables will not be available to the script.
  • Script errors can interrupt process execution
